claims.text: Host Permissions
`https://sso.garmin.com/*`
**Why**: Exchange your existing Garmin sign-in for a one-time service ticket. No password is entered or seen by the extension.

claims.text: `https://connectapi.garmin.com/*`

**Why**: Garmin's API host. The extension exchanges the ticket for tokens here, then makes every workout, activity, calendar and upload request with `Authorization: Bearer`. A request outside the allowlist of paths in the service worker is refused before it is sent.

claims.text: **Calendar write and delete**: When you place workouts on your Garmin Connect calendar from the Kaiord App, the extension calls two calendar endpoints on this host. `POST /workout-service/schedule/{workoutId}` places a library workout on a date, sending only that date. `DELETE /workout-service/schedule/{workoutScheduleId}` removes one calendar entry. The allowlist accepts both paths only with a numeric id, and neither path can delete a library workout.

claims.text: **Calendar read**: To check one workout's calendar entries, the extension calls `GET /calendar-service/year/{year}/month/{month}`. Garmin answers the whole month of your calendar; the extension keeps only the entries of that one workout, and passes back only each entry's id and date. Every other calendar item is discarded inside the extension and never reaches the Kaiord App.

claims.text: Kaiord for Garmin is the Chrome extension that connects the Kaiord App to Garmin Connect; its Chrome Web Store name is currently Kaiord Garmin Bridge. Here is how it handles data:

proof.title: handles push with gcn payload

claims.text: **OAuth Token**: The extension mints an OAuth token by reusing your existing Garmin single-sign-on session: it exchanges that session for a short-lived service ticket, then for an OAuth1 token, kept until it stops working, and an OAuth2 access token that expires and is renewed with the OAuth1 token. It stores both in `chrome.storage.local` so it can call Garmin's API on your behalf across service-worker restarts. To mint them it uses the consumer key and secret of Garmin's mobile app as published by the open-source garth project, not a key Garmin issued to Kaiord.

claims.text: **Calendar Placement**: When you push or send workouts from the Kaiord App, the extension places each workout on its date in your Garmin Connect calendar (a calendar write). When a workout moves to another day, it adds the new calendar entry first and then deletes the old entry that Kaiord itself placed and has since superseded (a calendar delete). It deletes only entries of workouts Kaiord sent, on the dates Kaiord placed them: an entry of that same workout that you added by hand on that date may be treated as Kaiord's and removed. It never deletes entries of other workouts, and never deletes library workouts.

claims.text: **Calendar Read, Filtered on Your Device**: The extension reads a month of your Garmin Connect calendar for three purposes only: to confirm a placement Garmin did not clearly confirm, to check the calendar before removing an entry Kaiord replaced, and to re-check entries whose earlier removal did not complete. The read is filtered inside the extension's service worker: only the entries of the workout being placed (each entry's schedule id and date) reach the Kaiord App. The rest of your calendar (activities, other workouts, titles, metrics) is discarded on your device, and nothing is sent to a Kaiord-operated server.
